EDIT: Some are wondering why I posted here, in this sub. I realize it may seem weird, but I posted to get the atheist POV on mild depression. I realize being an atheist doesn't make you a psychologist/psychiatrist/doctor, but that's not what I'm looking for - I'm simply asking other atheists how they deal with mild depression. I may have worded this whole thing incorrectly (nobody ever accused me of being a smart man), but my intent was to hear/read what others without theistic beliefs to to deal with depression.

I have always suffered from depression - nothing massive or debilitating, just a degradation of all enjoyment and a sour outlook on life for a shortish period. When I was a believer, obviously my magical flying jew took care of everything. Now however, things are very different. When I'm not depressed (which is the vast majority of the time, thank...natural order...), the fact that I am an inherently pointless collection of crap from across the universe fills me with joy - it's an indescribable relief to be able to fall back and say "this thing that's irritating me isn't a big deal, because in the grand scope of everything ever, nothing I have ever seen or experienced matters whatsoever".

When I am depressed...the very thing that comforts me, the thing that relieves my nerves, lessens my stress level, it worsens my depression. I mean, depression is often associated with a feeling of worthlessness in the first place - that kind of mood coupled with a joyfully held belief that you pointless isn't conducive to enjoying life or pulling yourself out of depression.

Now, I'm not suicidal or anything like that, it's just a shitty glum feeling that makes life suck for a bit - but how do you guys deal with it? I don't think medication is the best/only answer - mental meds are sketchy shit, I've watched my mother get put through the wringer her whole life with that shit, and it honestly doesn't look like we are any closer to figuring out the mind than we were 30 years ago (as far as mental illness I mean).

Are there any books to read that teach you how to manage depression, or are there things I can do that help bring you out of it, etc?

Do you get out much? Speaking from experience, it may help if you switch up your daily life's monotony. My depression subsided when I started dating and had excuses to go out and do things with people. Other than your reference to how you would defer sadness onto Jesus before your "conversion", why did you post this in the atheism subverse? Is it because you'd like the perspective of other atheists who have dealt with depression? If so, I don't have a lot of advice. What makes me happy - the fact there is no afterlife - probably doesn't make you as happy.

You could always consult Google about managing your depression, but if you feel this depression may worsen and could cause you to lead a debilitating life, maybe you should seek professional help.

A few things I've personally found or heard to be useful:

  1. Exercise. Regularly working out has been proven to be very beneficial for those with depression (Google will bring up some literature if you want to look). Not a cure all, and I know how difficult it can be to get out the door when you're down, but I feel it's worth the effort.

  2. Escapism. Personally, I try to find books, movies, shows, etc. that I can emotionally invest in and will make me laugh or even cry. Probably doesn't work for everyone, but I usually find that an outside source of strong emotion helps "lift the fog" sort to speak. Of course, escapism has its downsides if you let it consume too much of your time.

  3. Journaling/Other writing. I've heard of people keeping a journal to help with their depression. Some write out their thoughts when they're low to get it out of their system; others will record every positive thing they see/hear/experience then come back to it when they need a pick up.

Hope this helps, even if it's just a little bit.

Exercise. Meditation is great, but eating right and exercise are key. I broke my wrist a month ago. My wife and two kids went to Japan for six weeks without me (I don't get enough time off work to go with them every time) a few weeks ago, so I'm stuck at home, alone, with one hand. On Saturday my ride to the grocery store had something come up, so I walked 2.5 miles there, bought groceries (a reasonable amount, since I'm one-handed) and walked home. That 5 mile walk was likely the best thing I did that day.

Yeah, I love reading, playing video games, watching movies, etc...but because I'd gotten out and walked that day, the rest of the day was enjoyable. Had I been driven to/from the store and then spent the day inside, I probably would have felt mildly depressed myself.

I lived in Japan, a very secular country, for 10 years, and just walking to the store, station, etc, was enough of getting out and walking around. Now that I'm back in the states, it's mountain biking (or was, prior to my break) that is the main way I get outside and move around, but whether it's a sport/activity you love, the gym or just walking more, using your body will do wonders for your mind.

I hope that helps.
